title: Are Insider Trades Informative?
one_line: Across NYSE/AMEX/Nasdaq 1975-1995, insider purchases (not sales) predict returns, mainly at small firms; insiders are contrarian and time the market better than simple contrarian rules, with little market reaction when trades are reported.

findings.statement: Informative signal comes from purchases; sales show no predictive ability.
Insiders as a group forecast market moves better than simple contrarian strategies.

reported_results.headline: Across NYSE/AMEX/Nasdaq 1975-1995, insider purchases (not sales) predict returns, mainly at small firms; insiders are contrarian and time the market better than simple contrarian rules, with little market reaction when trades are reported.

tradable_edge: Stock-level; aggregate insider buying as a market-timing signal is untested here.
data_fit: Single-stock study — not testable on our ES/NQ data.
caveats: Read by Claude in a chat session (manual run 4), not by the weekly pipeline.
